title: Release quest-cli 0.8.0: version bump, CI-built platform binaries, qualification, tag
description: 29 commits sit on dev unpublished since the 0.7.1 hotfix freeze (2026-09-15), including QCLI-297's breaking removal-fails-loud change plus several Added/Fixed entries. The gap has cost the fleet three independent orchestrator-session investigations of the same already-fixed bug (--remove-note silent no-op) because every fresh session installs the published npm binary. QCLI-328 establishes that a Changed (breaking) CHANGELOG entry should correspond to at least a minor bump, so this releases as 0.8.0, not 0.7.2. Follow docs/runbooks/quest-cli-package-and-release.md: strings-then-bytes version bump (two commits), CI-built platform binaries via prepublication-qualification.yml dispatch, full qualification record, changelog finalization at tag time, native-execution receipt. Stops at 'ready to publish' -- the actual npm publish needs separate explicit owner authorization per that runbook's Prerequisites and is not covered by this task.

finalSummary:
quest-cli 0.8.0 is fully release-prepped and stops exactly where the runbook and the user's authorization boundary say it must: tagged, qualified, receipted, and NOT published.

WHAT SHIPPED. Six hand-edited version-string sites plus all six platform manifests moved to 0.8.0 (PR #182), a Tracker-integrity CI defect found mid-release was fixed first because it was blocking (PR #183, QCLI-333), CHANGELOG.md's Unreleased heading was renamed to 0.8.0 with a fresh empty successor (PR #184), and v0.8.0 was tagged and pushed at the resulting commit 9d91fc3.

HOW IT WAS VERIFIED. bun run check: exit 0, 568 pass/0 fail across 66 files. The same 21-gate qualification script CI's source-gates job runs (scripts/qualification/prepublish.mjs) was also run locally with the native darwin-arm64 candidate smoke enabled: all 21 gates passed, including a clean install from packed tarballs (never the working-tree binary, so no SIGKILL-hazard execution occurred) exercising --version, manifest, task create/list, sqlite-smoke and migration-smoke end to end. prepublication-qualification.yml was dispatched against the v0.8.0 tag (run 35287130169): source-gates, all six immutable-candidates targets (each attesting the COMMITTED artifact rather than rebuilding, since Bun's --compile output isn't reproducible), candidate-bundle, and native-execution-receipt all completed success. The downloaded receipt passed `bun run receipt:require`, confirming it binds 0.8.0 at 9d91fc3 across all six platforms.

ONE THING LEARNED THAT WASN'T ALREADY WRITTEN DOWN. The tag push's own push-triggered workflow run and the explicit `gh workflow run --ref v0.8.0` dispatch share the same concurrency group (both resolve `github.ref` to `refs/tags/v0.8.0`), so the push-triggered run was correctly cancelled when the dispatch started five seconds later. That is the runbook's documented "dispatch explicitly rather than relying on the tag push" behavior working as intended, not a failure -- but it is worth knowing so a future release doesn't mistake the cancelled push run for a broken one.

WHAT THIS TASK DELIBERATELY DID NOT DO. dev sits at 9d91fc3, five commits ahead of main (954cd36) -- unlike QCLI-294 (0.7.0), this task's own acceptance criteria never named a dev-to-main promotion, so none was performed; that is an open question for the orchestrator/owner to sequence, not a gap in this task's scope. Step 7, the actual npm publish, was not attempted and needs the owner's own direct authorization per the runbook's Prerequisites and Tier-3 in opum-fleet-operating.md -- not the orchestrator's relayed instruction, which named this same boundary explicitly when handing the task back.
